title: Hello, Minato
tagline: Introduce yourself, ask who someone is, and say whose things are whose.
hook: Noa steps off the train in Minato with one suitcase and a lot of nerves. In a few minutes you'll have the words and the three tiny particles that make a first conversation work.
goals: Say who you are with は and です
Turn any statement into a question with か
Link two nouns with の and add さん politely
vocab: よろしくおねがいします
よろしくおねがいします

points.title: 〜は〜です
explain: は is a spotlight. It marks the topic: the thing you are about to say something about. Read it as "as for A...".
です is the polite full stop. It closes the sentence and tells the listener you're being respectful. There is no separate word for "am / is / are".

examples.ja: レオさんは|ブラジル人です。

points.tip: Japanese drops "I" all the time once the topic is clear. 学生です alone can mean "I am a student".
points.watch: As a particle, は is pronounced "wa". In はじめまして it stays "ha".

points.title: 〜か
points.formula: A は B ですか
explain: Add か to the end and the sentence becomes a yes/no question. There's no word-order change and normally no question mark needed.
Answer with はい (yes) or いいえ (no), then repeat the key part.

examples.ja: ノアさんは|カナダ人|ですか。
いいえ、|アメリカ人です。

points.tip: か is only for asking. Say it with rising tone and you sound curious, not rude.
points.watch: Don't put か in the middle. It always closes the question.

points.title: 〜の
points.gist: A's B / the B of A.
explain: の links two nouns. The first one describes or owns the second: 大学の学生 is a student of the university.
It works for belonging (わたしの名前), affiliation (大学の先生) and subject (日本語の先生).

examples.ja: わたしの|名前は|ノアです。
みなと大学の|留学生です。
examples.en: I'm an exchange student at Minato University.

examples.ja: 森先生の|専攻は|何ですか。

points.tip: Add さん after a name when you talk about someone else. Never add it to your own name.
points.watch: If the second noun is obvious you can drop it: それはわたしのです ("that's mine").

drills.q: Which sentence politely says "Leo is Brazilian"?
options: レオさんは ブラジル人です。
レオさんを ブラジル人です。
レオさんは ブラジル人。です
レオさんの ブラジル人です。
drills.why: は for the topic, then the noun, then です.

drills.ja: ノアさんは カナダ人です＿。
drills.why: か at the end makes it a question.

drills.q: Someone asks 学生ですか。 You are a student. What do you say?
drills.why: はい means yes; repeat the answer with です.

drills.ja: わたし＿名前は ノアです。
drills.why: の links わたし and 名前.

drills.en: I'm an exchange student at Minato University.

drills.prompt: Type the reading of 先生 (teacher) in hiragana.
Type the reading of 友だち (friend) in hiragana.

drills.why: 一 = one, 年生 = school-year student.

drills.ja: ハナさん＿ 二年生ですか。
drills.why: は marks Hana as the topic of the question.
